topic: In Practice issue 13: sleep drive and a steady wake time
text:
In Practice, issue 13, is now live: sleep drive and a steady wake time.

In Practice is our one-page research update for GPs and anyone working in primary care. This month's theme: sleep drive builds from the moment a person wakes and is spent by sleep, so naps and sleep-ins lower it and caffeine masks its signal.

What the issue covers:

1. How sleep drive builds. An illustration based on the two-process model shows how a sleep-in or an afternoon nap leaves less sleep pressure at bedtime.

2. Adenosine and caffeine. Adenosine is one of several signals that build with time awake. Caffeine blocks its receptors, and research pooling many studies linked it with less total sleep.

3. A steady wake time. Australia's 2026 joint position statement names CBTi as first line, and bedtime restriction with a consistent rise time works directly with sleep drive.

4. Three consult questions and a short guide on when to consider a referral.

Each issue comes with a patient handout, this month on sleep drive and a steady wake time. Both are free to download from our referrers page:
https://equalpsychology.com.au/referrers#in-practice
